title.en: Volume 151 Biographies 39: Ru Chang, Yan Zhenzhi, Zhang Dan, Wang Dun, Zheng Ci, Guo Zi, Lu Zhen, Li Zhigang, Fang Bin, Wu Zhong, Liu Guan
title.raw: 卷一百五十一 列傳第三十九 茹瑺 嚴震直 張紞 王鈍 鄭賜 郭資 呂震 李至剛 方賓 吳中 劉觀 Volume 151 Biographies 39: Ru Chang, Yan Zhenzhi, Zhang Dan, Wang Dun, Zheng Ci, Guo Zi, Lu Zhen, Li Zhigang, Fang Bin, Wu Zhong, Liu Guan

sentences.zh: 茹常嚴震直張紞

translations.literal: Ru Chang, Yan Zhenzhi, Zhang Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Chang, Yan Zhenzhi, and Zhang Dan.

sentences.zh: （毛泰亨）〉

translations.literal: (Mao Taiheng)]〉
translations.idiomatic: (Mao Taiheng)]〉

sentences.zh: 王鈍鄭賜郭資呂震李至剛方賓吳中劉觀

translations.literal: Wang Dun, Zheng Ci, Guo Zi, Lu Zhen, Li Zhigang, Fang Bin, Wu Zhong, Liu Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, Zheng Ci, Guo Zi, Lu Zhen, Li Zhigang, Fang Bin, Wu Zhong, and Liu Guan.

sentences.zh: 茹常，衡山人。

translations.literal: Ru Chang was a native of Hengshan.
translations.idiomatic: Ru Chang was from Hengshan.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，由監生除承敕郎，歷通政使。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, through the status of a student of the Directorate of Education he was appointed Chengchi Lang, and rose to Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he entered service as a Directorate student, was appointed a drafter of imperial rescripts, and eventually became Commissioner of the Office of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 勤於職，太祖賢之。

translations.literal: He was diligent in his duties, and the Taizu Emperor regarded him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent in office, he won Taizu's esteem.

sentences.zh: 二十三年拜右副都御史，又試兵部尚書，尋實授，加太子少保。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, then was tried out as Minister of War, soon after given the substantive post, and added as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three of the reign he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, then given a probationary appointment as Minister of War, which soon became permanent, with the additional title of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 及惠帝即位，改吏部，與黃子澄不相能，刑部尚書暴昭發其贓罪，出掌河南布政司事。

translations.literal: When the Hui Emperor took the throne, he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; he did not get along with Huang Zicheng, and the Minister of Justice Bao Zhao exposed his corruption, so he was sent out to administer the Henan Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui acceded, Chang was moved to the Ministry of Personnel but clashed with Huang Zicheng; Minister of Justice Bao Zhao then exposed his graft, and he was posted to head the Henan provincial administration.

sentences.zh: 尋復召為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned back as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 燕兵至龍潭，帝遣常及曹國公李景隆、都督同知王佐詣燕軍議和。

translations.literal: When the Yan army reached Longtan, the Emperor sent Chang together with the Duke of Cao, Li Jinglong, and the Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Wang Zuo to the Yan army to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yan forces reached Longtan, the emperor dispatched Chang with the Duke of Cao, Li Jinglong, and Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief Wang Zuo to sue for peace with the rebel army.

sentences.zh: 常等見成祖，伏地流汗，不能發一言。

translations.literal: When Chang and the others met the Chengzu Emperor, they prostrated themselves, sweat streaming, and could not utter a single word.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and his party met the Prince of Yan and prostrated themselves, sweating so profusely they could not speak.

sentences.zh: 成祖曰：「公等言即言耳，何懼至是。」

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor said: "If you gentlemen have something to say, then say it—why fear to such a degree."
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "Speak if you have something to say—why such terror."

sentences.zh: 久之，乃言奉詔割地講和。

translations.literal: After a long while they finally said that they had been commanded to cede territory and make peace.
translations.idiomatic: At length they stated their commission: to cede territory and conclude peace.

sentences.zh: 成祖笑曰：「吾無罪而削為庶人，今救死，何以地為！

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor laughed and said: "I was guiltless yet reduced to a commoner; now I fight for my life—what need have I of land!
translations.idiomatic: He laughed and replied, "I was stripped of my rank though guilty of nothing; now I fight for my life—what use is land to me!

sentences.zh: 且皇考封諸子，已各有分地矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, when my late father enfeoffed his sons, each already received his allotted domain.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when my late father enfeoffed his sons, each already had his own domain.

sentences.zh: 其縛奸臣來，吾即解甲謁孝陵歸藩。」

translations.literal: If you bind up the treacherous ministers and bring them here, I will at once lay down my arms, pay homage at the Xiaoling Mausoleum, and return to my fief."
translations.idiomatic: Bind up the traitorous ministers and deliver them, and I will lay down my arms, pay homage at my father's tomb, and return to my fief."

sentences.zh: 常等唯唯頓首還。

translations.literal: Chang and the others murmured assent, kowtowed, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Chang and his companions murmured agreement, kowtowed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 還朝，坐不送趙王，遣歸裏。

translations.literal: On returning to court, he was punished for failing to escort the Prince of Zhao and was sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court he was punished for failing to escort the Prince of Zhao and sent home.

sentences.zh: 既而為家人所訟，逮至京。

translations.literal: Before long he was sued by members of his household and brought to the capital under arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward his own household sued him, and he was brought to the capital.

sentences.zh: 釋還。

translations.literal: He was released and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: He was released and sent home again.

sentences.zh: 過長沙不謁谷王，王以為言。

translations.literal: Passing through Changsha he did not call on the Prince of Gu, and the prince reported this.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Changsha he failed to call on the Prince of Gu, who complained of the slight.

sentences.zh: 時方重藩王禮，谷王又開金川門有功，帝意向之。

translations.literal: At that time the court was laying great weight on the rites owed to princes of the blood, and the Prince of Gu had further rendered service by opening the Jinchuan Gate, so the Emperor inclined to believe him.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then emphasizing princely protocol, and the Prince of Gu had the added credit of opening the Jinchuan Gate, so the emperor gave weight to his account.

sentences.zh: 陳瑛遂劾常違祖制，逮下錦衣獄。

translations.literal: Chen Ying thereupon impeached Chang for violating ancestral institutions, and he was arrested and sent down to the Brocade Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ying then impeached Chang for violating ancestral institutions, and he was imprisoned in the Brocade Guard jail.

sentences.zh: 常知不免，命子銓市毒藥，服之死。

translations.literal: Knowing he could not escape, Chang ordered his son Quan to buy poison; he took it and died.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing no escape, Chang had his son Quan buy poison and took it to die.

sentences.zh: 時永樂七年二月也。

translations.literal: This was in the second month of the seventh year of the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: This was in the second month of Yongle year seven.

sentences.zh: 法司劾銓毒其父，請以謀殺父母論。

translations.literal: The judicial offices impeached Quan for poisoning his father and requested that he be judged under the statute for plotting to murder one's parents.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices charged Quan with poisoning his father and sought conviction for plotting parricide.

sentences.zh: 後以銓實承父命，減死，與兄弟家屬二十七人謫戍廣西河池。

translations.literal: Later, because Quan had truly carried out his father's command, his sentence was reduced from death; he and twenty-seven brothers and dependents were banished to garrison duty at Hechi in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Because Quan had acted only on his father's orders, the death sentence was commuted, and he with twenty-seven brothers and dependents was exiled to garrison duty at Hechi in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 仁宗立，釋還。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, they were released and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong acceded, they were released and allowed to return.

sentences.zh: 宣宗與所沒田廬。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor restored the confiscated fields and dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong restored their confiscated fields and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 瑺居官謹慎，謙和有容。

translations.literal: Chang in office was cautious, modest, and accommodating.
translations.idiomatic: In office Chang had been careful, modest, and forbearing.

sentences.zh: 其死也，人頗惜之。

translations.literal: At his death many regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: His death was widely regretted.

sentences.zh: 嚴震直，字子敏，烏程人。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenzhi, style name Zimin, was a native of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenzhi, whose style was Zimin, was from Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 洪武時以富民擇糧長，歲部糧萬石至京師，無後期，帝才之。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, as a wealthy household head he was selected as grain chief; each year he delivered ten thousand piculs of grain to the capital without ever being late, and the Emperor recognized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he was chosen as grain chief from among the wealthy households; year after year he delivered ten thousand piculs to the capital without a single late shipment, and the emperor took note of his ability.

sentences.zh: 二十三年特授通政司參議，再遷為工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was specially appointed Councillor of the Office of Transmission, and was promoted again to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three he received a special appointment as Councillor of the Office of Transmission and was soon promoted to Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 二十六年六月進尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-sixth year he was advanced to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year twenty-six he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷事營建，集天下工匠於京師，凡二十余萬戶。

translations.literal: At that time the court was engaged in construction projects and had gathered artisans from throughout the realm at the capital, totaling more than two hundred thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then absorbed in construction and had assembled more than two hundred thousand artisan households from across the empire at the capital.

sentences.zh: 震直請戶役一人，書其姓名、所業於官，有役則按籍更番召之，役者稱便。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi requested that one person per household be registered, with name and trade written down at the office; when labor was needed they would be summoned in rotation according to the register, and those conscripted said this was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi proposed registering one man per household with name and trade on file, then calling them in rotation when labor was needed—a system the conscripts found workable.

sentences.zh: 鄉民訴其弟侄不法，帝付震直訊。

translations.literal: Villagers from his home district accused his younger brother and nephews of unlawful conduct; the Emperor entrusted the investigation to Zhenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: When villagers from his home district accused his brother and nephews of misconduct, the emperor put Zhenzhi in charge of the inquiry.

sentences.zh: 具獄上，帝以為不欺，赦其弟侄。

translations.literal: He completed the case and submitted it; the Emperor, believing he had not concealed anything, pardoned his brother and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the full findings, and the emperor, judging that he had not shielded his kin, pardoned the brother and nephews.

sentences.zh: 已，坐事降御史，數雪冤獄。

translations.literal: Later, because of an offense he was demoted to censor, and repeatedly cleared wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: He was later demoted to censor for an offense but repeatedly secured reversals of wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 二十八年討龍州，使震直偕尚書任亨泰諭安南。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year, when Longzhou was attacked, Zhenzhi was sent together with the Minister Ren Hengtai to instruct Annam.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-eight, during the campaign against Longzhou, he was sent with Minister Ren Hengtai to deliver instructions to Annam.

sentences.zh: 還，條奏利病，稱旨。

translations.literal: On his return he submitted a detailed memorial on benefits and harms, which accorded with the Emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he memorialized point by point on what helped and what harmed the realm, and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋命修廣西興安縣靈渠。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to repair the Ling Canal in Xing'an County, Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to repair the Ling Canal at Xing'an in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 審度地勢，導湘、漓二江，浚渠五千余丈，築渼潭及龍母祠土堤百五十余丈，又增高中江石堤，建陡閘三十有六，鑿去灘石之礙舟者，漕運悉通。

translations.literal: He surveyed the terrain, channeled the Xiang and Li rivers, dredged the canal for more than five thousand zhang, built earthen dikes at Meitan and the Dragon Mother Shrine totaling more than one hundred fifty zhang, further raised the stone dike at the middle reach of the Jiang, constructed thirty-six steep locks, and cut away reef stones that obstructed boats, so that grain transport was entirely unblocked.
translations.idiomatic: Surveying the terrain, he directed the Xiang and Li rivers, dredged more than five thousand zhang of canal, built one hundred fifty-odd zhang of earthen dikes at Meitan and the Dragon Mother Shrine, raised the mid-river stone dike, erected thirty-six pound locks, and removed reef stones that blocked shipping, so that grain transport ran clear throughout.

sentences.zh: 歸奏，帝稱善。

translations.literal: On returning he reported, and the Emperor praised the work.
translations.idiomatic: He reported on his return, and the emperor commended the achievement.

sentences.zh: 三十年二月疏言：「廣東舊運鹽八十五萬余引於廣西，召商中買。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirtieth year he memorialized: "Guangdong formerly transported more than eight hundred fifty thousand salt certificates' worth of salt to Guangxi, summoning merchants to bid for it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year thirty he memorialized: "Guangdong formerly shipped more than 850,000 salt certificates' worth of salt to Guangxi for merchants to bid on.

sentences.zh: 今終年所運，才十之一。

translations.literal: Now what is transported in a full year is only one-tenth of that.
translations.idiomatic: In a full year today barely a tenth of that volume moves.

sentences.zh: 請分三十萬八千余引貯廣東，別募商入粟廣西之糧衛所，支鹽廣東，鬻之江西南安、贛州、吉安、臨江四府便。」

translations.literal: I request that more than three hundred eight thousand certificates be stored in Guangdong, that merchants be separately recruited to deliver grain to the grain guards in Guangxi, that they draw salt in Guangdong, and that it be sold in the four prefectures of Nan'an, Ganzhou, Ji'an, and Linjiang in Jiangxi, which would be convenient."
translations.idiomatic: I propose storing 308,000-odd certificates in Guangdong, recruiting merchants separately to deliver grain to Guangxi grain guards, issuing salt in Guangdong, and selling it in the Jiangxi prefectures of Nan'an, Ganzhou, Ji'an, and Linjiang, which would be far more workable."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 廣鹽行於江西自此始。

translations.literal: Guangdong salt circulating in Jiangxi began from this.
translations.idiomatic: This was how Guangdong salt first came to be marketed in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 其年四月擢右都御史，尋復為工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of that year he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief, and before long was again made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of that year he was made Right Censor-in-Chief and soon restored as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 建文中，嘗督餉山東，已而致仕。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he once supervised provisions in Shandong, and later retired.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen he had supervised grain shipments in Shandong before retiring.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，召見，命以故官巡視山西。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor took the throne, he was summoned for an audience and ordered to tour Shanxi in his former capacity.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu acceded he was summoned and sent to inspect Shanxi in his former ministerial capacity.

sentences.zh: 至澤州，病卒。

translations.literal: Reaching Zezhou, he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died at Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 張紞，字昭季，富平人。

translations.literal: Zhang Dan, style name Zhaoji, was a native of Fuping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dan, whose style was Zhaoji, was from Fuping.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，舉明經。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he was recommended in the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 為東宮侍書，累遷試左通政。

translations.literal: He served as attendant scribe to the Eastern Palace and was promoted in stages to Acting Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a scribe in the heir apparent's household and rose to acting Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 十五年，雲南平，出為左參政。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, when Yunnan was pacified, he went out as Left Administrative Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifteen, after Yunnan was pacified, he was posted as Left Administrative Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，帝賦詩二章賜之。

translations.literal: On taking leave at court the Emperor composed two poems and bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor composed two poems and bestowed them on him.

sentences.zh: 歷左布政使。

translations.literal: He rose to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 二十年春入覲，治行為天下第一，特令吏部勿考。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twentieth year he came to court for an audience; his record of governance ranked first in the realm, and he was specially ordered that the Ministry of Personnel should not examine him.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year twenty he presented himself at court; his governance ranked first in the empire, and he was specially exempted from the Ministry of Personnel's performance review.

sentences.zh: 賜璽書曰：「曩者討平西南，命官撫守，爾紞實先往，於今五年。

translations.literal: An imperial letter with the seal was granted, saying: "Formerly, when the southwest was pacified, officials were appointed to govern and guard it; you, Dan, were in fact the first to go, and it is now five years.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial sealed letter read: "When the southwest was pacified I appointed officials to govern it; you, Dan, were the first to go, and five years have passed.

sentences.zh: 諸蠻聽服，誠信相孚，克恭乃職，不待考而朕知其功出天下十二牧上。

translations.literal: The various Man peoples heed and submit; sincerity and trust are mutual; you respectfully fulfill your duties—without examination I know your achievement surpasses the twelve provincial governors of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes obey, trust is mutual, and you discharge your duties with due reverence; without any review I know your merit surpasses every provincial governor in the land.

sentences.zh: 故嘉爾績，命爾仍治滇南。

translations.literal: Therefore I commend your merit and command you to continue governing southern Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore commend your record and command you to continue governing southern Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 往，欽哉。」

translations.literal: Go, and reverently heed this."
translations.idiomatic: Go, and take this charge to heart."

sentences.zh: 紞在滇凡十七年，土地貢賦、法令條格皆所裁定。

translations.literal: Dan was in Yunnan altogether seventeen years; land taxes, tribute, statutes, and regulations were all determined by him.
translations.idiomatic: Dan spent seventeen years in Yunnan, setting land assessments, tribute schedules, statutes, and regulations.

sentences.zh: 民間喪祭冠婚鹹有定制，務變其俗。

translations.literal: For funerals, sacrifices, capping ceremonies, and weddings among the people he all had fixed regulations, striving to transform their customs.
translations.idiomatic: He prescribed fixed forms for funerals, sacrifices, capping, and weddings among the populace, striving to reshape local custom.

sentences.zh: 滇人遵用之。

translations.literal: The people of Yunnan followed and used them.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yunnan followed them.

sentences.zh: 朝士董倫、王景輩謫其地，皆接以禮意。

translations.literal: Court gentlemen such as Dong Lun and Wang Jing, banished to that region, were all received by him with courteous regard.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials banished there, such as Dong Lun and Wang Jing, he always received with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，召為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When the Hui Emperor took the throne, he was summoned as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hui acceded, he was recalled as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 詔征遺逸士集闕下。

translations.literal: An edict was issued to summon reclusive scholars to assemble below the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned reclusive scholars to the capital.

sentences.zh: 紞所選用，皆當其才。

translations.literal: Those whom Dan selected and employed were all suited to their talents.
translations.idiomatic: Every man Dan recommended was well matched to his abilities.

sentences.zh: 會修《太祖實錄》，命試翰林編纂官，紞奏楊士奇第一。

translations.literal: When the 《Veritable Records of the Taizu Emperor》 were being compiled, he was ordered to test the Hanlin compilation officers; Dan reported Yang Shiqi as first.
translations.idiomatic: During the compilation of the 《Veritable Records of the Taizu Emperor》 he was asked to examine Hanlin compilers and ranked Yang Shiqi first.

sentences.zh: 士奇由是知名。

translations.literal: Shiqi thereby became renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi thereby came to prominence.

sentences.zh: 成祖入京師，錄中朝奸臣二十九人，紞與焉。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor entered the capital, a register was made of twenty-nine treacherous ministers of the central court, and Dan was among them.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu entered the capital, twenty-nine Jianwen ministers were listed as traitors, Dan among them.

sentences.zh: 以茹常言，宥仍故職。

translations.literal: On Ru Chang's word he was pardoned and kept in his former post.
translations.idiomatic: On Ru Chang's intercession he was pardoned and kept in office.

sentences.zh: 無何，帝臨朝而嘆，咎建文時之改官制者。

translations.literal: Before long, at court the Emperor sighed and blamed those who had altered the official system during the Jianwen reign.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, at court the emperor sighed and blamed those who had reformed the bureaucracy under Jianwen.

sentences.zh: 乃令紞及戶部尚書王鈍解職務，月給半俸，居京師。

translations.literal: He then ordered Dan and the Minister of Revenue Wang Dun to resign their duties, receiving half salary each month and residing in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered Dan and Minister of Revenue Wang Dun to step down, granting half pay and requiring them to remain in the capital.

sentences.zh: 紞懼，自經於吏部後堂，妻子相率投池中死。

translations.literal: Dan, in fear, hanged himself in the rear hall of the Ministry of Personnel; his wife and children in succession threw themselves into a pool and died.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Dan hanged himself in the ministry's rear hall; his wife and children then drowned themselves in a pool one after another.

sentences.zh: 紞在吏部，值變官制，小吏張祖言曰：「高皇帝立法創制，規模甚遠。

translations.literal: When Dan was at the Ministry of Personnel, at the time of changing the official system, a minor clerk named Zhang Zu said: "The Gaozu Emperor in legislating and establishing institutions had a vision of very far reach.
translations.idiomatic: While Dan was at the Ministry of Personnel during the bureaucratic reforms, a junior clerk named Zhang Zu said, "When the founding emperor legislated and established institutions, his vision reached far ahead.

sentences.zh: 今更之，未必勝，徒滋人口，願公力持之。」

translations.literal: To change them now may not necessarily be better, and will only multiply talk; I hope Your Excellency will strive to uphold the old system."
translations.idiomatic: Today's changes may not improve on them and will only breed talk; I urge you to hold firm against them."

sentences.zh: 紞不能用，然心賢祖，奏為京衛知事。

translations.literal: Dan could not adopt this, yet in his heart he regarded Zu as worthy and memorialized to make him a registrar of the capital guards.
translations.idiomatic: Dan could not heed him, yet admired him inwardly and had him appointed registrar of the capital guards.

sentences.zh: 後紞死，屬吏無敢視者，唯祖經紀其喪。

translations.literal: Later, when Dan died, none of his subordinate officials dared to attend; only Zu managed his funeral.
translations.idiomatic: After Dan's death none of his subordinates dared attend the body; only Zu arranged the funeral.

sentences.zh: 世傳燕師入京，紞即自經死；

translations.literal: The world transmits that when the Yan army entered the capital, Dan at once hanged himself and died;
translations.idiomatic: Popular tradition holds that when the Yan army entered the capital Dan hanged himself at once;

sentences.zh: 嚴震直奉使至雲南，遇建文君悲愴吞金死。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenzhi on a mission reached Yunnan and encountered the Jianwen sovereign, who in grief and anguish swallowed gold and died.
translations.idiomatic: and that Yan Zhenzhi on a mission to Yunnan encountered the Jianwen emperor, who in grief swallowed gold and died.

sentences.zh: 考諸國史，非其實也。

translations.literal: Examining the dynastic histories, this is not the fact.
translations.idiomatic: Examination of the official histories shows neither story to be true.

sentences.zh: 時有毛泰亨者，建文時為吏部侍郎，與紞同事。

translations.literal: At that time there was one Mao Taiheng, who during the Jianwen reign was Vice Minister of Personnel and served together with Dan.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Mao Taiheng, who under Jianwen had been Vice Minister of Personnel and served alongside Dan.

sentences.zh: 紞死，泰亨亦死。

translations.literal: When Dan died, Taiheng also died.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan died, Taiheng died as well.

sentences.zh: 王鈍，字士魯，太康人。

translations.literal: Wang Dun, style name Shilu, was a native of Taikang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, whose style was Shilu, was from Taikang.

sentences.zh: 元末猗氏縣尹。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he was magistrate of Yishi County.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he had been magistrate of Yishi County.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，征授禮部主事，歷官福建參政，以廉慎聞。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he was summoned and appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Rites, served in posts culminating as Fujian Administrative Commissioner, and was known for integrity and prudence.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he was summoned to a principal clerkship in the Ministry of Rites and rose to Fujian Administrative Commissioner, renowned for integrity and prudence.

sentences.zh: 遣諭麓川，卻其贈。

translations.literal: Sent to instruct Luchuan, he declined their gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to instruct Luchuan he refused their gifts.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「不受恐遠人疑貳。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "If you do not accept them, I fear the distant peoples will suspect disloyalty."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "If you refuse them, the distant peoples may suspect disloyalty."

sentences.zh: 鈍乃受之。

translations.literal: Dun then accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Dun then accepted them.

sentences.zh: 還至雲南，輸之官庫。

translations.literal: On returning to Yunnan he turned them in to the government storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Yunnan he deposited them in the government treasury.

sentences.zh: 二十三年遷浙江左布政使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three he was transferred to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 在浙十年，名與張紞埒。

translations.literal: He was in Zhejiang ten years, his reputation equal to Zhang Dan's.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years in Zhejiang left his reputation equal to Zhang Dan's.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗稱於朝，以勸庶僚。

translations.literal: The Emperor once praised him at court to encourage the various officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once praised him at court as an example to the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 建文初，拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwen reign he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Jianwen he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 成祖入，逾城走，為邏卒所執。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor entered, he fled over the city wall and was seized by patrol soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu entered the capital, Dun fled over the city wall but was seized by patrol soldiers.

sentences.zh: 詔仍故官。

translations.literal: An edict restored him to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored him to his former office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與紞俱罷。

translations.literal: Before long he was dismissed together with Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was dismissed along with Zhang Dan.

sentences.zh: 尋命同工部尚書嚴震直等分巡山西、河南、陜西、山東，又同新昌伯唐雲經理北平屯種。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered together with the Minister of Works Yan Zhenzhi and others to tour separately Shanxi, Henan, Shaanxi, and Shandong, and also together with the Baron of Xinchang, Tang Yun, to oversee garrison farming around Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered with Minister of Works Yan Zhenzhi and others to tour Shanxi, Henan, Shaanxi, and Shandong, and with the Baron of Xinchang, Tang Yun, to oversee garrison farming in Beiping.

sentences.zh: 承制再上疏言事，皆允行。

translations.literal: By imperial commission he again submitted memorials on affairs, and all were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioned by the throne, he memorialized again on policy matters, and every proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年四月賜敕以布政使致仕。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year of the Yongle reign an imperial letter was granted permitting him to retire as provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Yongle year two he received an imperial letter permitting retirement at his former rank of provincial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 既歸，郁郁死。

translations.literal: After returning home he died in dejection.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he died of melancholy.

sentences.zh: 子淪，永樂四年進士。

translations.literal: His son Lun passed the metropolitan examination in the fourth year of the Yongle reign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lun passed the metropolitan examination in Yongle year four.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時遷鄭王府左長史，數以禮諫王。

translations.literal: During the Renzong reign he was transferred to Left Administrator of the Prince of Zheng's household and repeatedly admonished the prince according to ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Under Renzong he became Left Administrator of the Prince of Zheng's household and repeatedly admonished the prince on ritual grounds.

sentences.zh: 嘗擬荀卿《成相篇》，撰十二章以獻。

translations.literal: He once modeled himself on Xunzi's "Chengxiang" chapter and composed twelve chapters to present.
translations.idiomatic: He once modeled Xunzi's "Chengxiang" chapter and composed twelve chapters for presentation.

sentences.zh: 語切，與王不合。

translations.literal: His language was pointed, and he did not get along with the prince.
translations.idiomatic: His language was blunt, and he fell out with the prince.

sentences.zh: 召改戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned and transferred to Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and made a director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，擢戶部右侍郎，巡撫浙江，有惠政。

translations.literal: When the Yingzong Emperor took the throne, he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue and toured Zhejiang as grand coordinator, enacting benevolent policies.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong acceded he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, toured Zhejiang as grand coordinator, and won a reputation for benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 母喪起復，入覲，留攝部事。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning for his mother, he came to court for an audience and was retained to administer the ministry's affairs in the minister's absence.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning for his mother, he presented himself at court and was kept on to administer the ministry in the minister's stead.

sentences.zh: 尋以老乞歸，卒。

translations.literal: Before long, citing old age, he requested to return home and died.
translations.idiomatic: He soon asked to retire on grounds of age and died.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，代李至剛為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year he replaced Li Zhigang as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of year three he replaced Li Zhigang as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，西域貢佛舍利，賜因請釋囚。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, when the Western Regions presented Buddhist relics, Ci thereupon requested the release of prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year four, when the Western Regions presented Buddhist relics, Ci asked that prisoners be released.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「梁武、元順溺佛教，有罪者不刑，紀綱大壞，此豈可效！」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Emperor Wu of Liang and Emperor Shun of Yuan were drowned in Buddhism; criminals went unpunished and state discipline was greatly ruined—how can this be imitated!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Emperor Wu of Liang and Emperor Shun of Yuan were drowned in Buddhism; criminals went unpunished and state discipline collapsed—how can we imitate that!"

sentences.zh: 是年六月朔，日當食，陰雲不見，賜請賀。

translations.literal: In that year on the first day of the sixth month an eclipse was due, but clouds obscured the sky and it could not be seen; Ci requested congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: That year on the first day of the sixth month an eclipse was due, but clouds hid the sky; Ci asked that congratulations be offered.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 賜言「宋盛時嘗行之。」

translations.literal: Ci said, "In the flourishing age of the Song this was once done."
translations.idiomatic: Ci said, "In the Song at its height this was done."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下大矣，京師不見，如天下見之何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The realm is vast; if the capital did not see it, what of the places throughout the realm that did?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "The realm is vast; if the capital did not see it, what of all the places that did?"

sentences.zh: 卒不許。

translations.literal: In the end it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he still refused.

sentences.zh: 賜為人頗和厚，然不識大體，帝意輕之。

translations.literal: Ci as a man was rather mild and generous, yet he did not grasp the larger pattern, and the Emperor held him in light esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Ci was mild and generous by nature but lacked a sense of the larger pattern, and the emperor thought little of him.

sentences.zh: 為同官趙羾所間，六年六月憂悸卒。

translations.literal: Slandered by his colleague Zhao Huo, he died in the sixth month of the sixth year from anxiety and dread.
translations.idiomatic: Slandered by his colleague Zhao Huo, he died in the sixth month of year six from anxiety and dread.

sentences.zh: 帝疑其自盡。

translations.literal: The Emperor suspected he had killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor suspected suicide.

sentences.zh: 楊士奇曰：「賜有疾數日，惶懼不敢求退。

translations.literal: Yang Shiqi said: "Ci had been ill for several days, fearful and not daring to request retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shiqi said, "Ci had been ill for days, too fearful to ask to retire.

sentences.zh: 昨立右順門，力不支仆地，口鼻有噓無吸。」

translations.literal: Yesterday, standing at the Right Shun Gate, his strength failed and he fell prostrate; there was exhalation from his mouth and nose but no inhalation."
translations.idiomatic: Yesterday at the Right Shun Gate his strength failed and he collapsed; he exhaled but could not draw breath."

sentences.zh: 語未竟，帝曰：「微汝言，幾誤疑賜。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking, the Emperor said: "But for your words, I would nearly have wrongly suspected Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Before he finished, the emperor said, "But for you I would nearly have wrongly suspected Ci.

sentences.zh: 賜固善人，才短耳。」

translations.literal: Ci was indeed a good man, only short in talent."
translations.idiomatic: Ci was a good man, only limited in talent."

sentences.zh: 命予葬祭。

translations.literal: He ordered funeral rites and sacrifices granted.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered funeral rites and sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年贈太子少保，謚文安。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Hongxi reign he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous title Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi year one he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 郭資，武安人。

translations.literal: Guo Zi was a native of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zi was from Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of the Hongwu reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Hongwu year eighteen.

sentences.zh: 累官北平左布政使，陰附於成祖。

translations.literal: Rising through offices to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Beiping, he secretly attached himself to the Chengzu Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Beiping and secretly aligned himself with Chengzu.

sentences.zh: 及兵起，張昺等死，資與左參政孫瑜、按察司副使墨麟、僉事呂震率先降，呼萬歲。

translations.literal: When the army rose, Zhang Bing and others died; Zi together with Left Administrative Vice Commissioner Sun Yu, Vice Commissioner of the Surveillance Commission Mo Lin, and Assistant Commissioner Lu Zhen were the first to surrender, crying "Long live the Emperor!"
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out and Zhang Bing and others were killed, Zi with Left Vice Commissioner Sun Yu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner Mo Lin, and Assistant Commissioner Lu Zhen were the first to surrender, crying "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 成祖悅，命輔世子居守。

translations.literal: The Chengzu Emperor was pleased and ordered him to assist the heir apparent in remaining to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu was pleased and ordered him to assist the heir apparent in holding the capital.

sentences.zh: 資治錢谷有能稱，仁宗嘗以問楊士奇。

translations.literal: Zi in managing revenue and grain had a reputation for ability; the Renzong Emperor once asked Yang Shiqi about him.
translations.idiomatic: Zi had a reputation for competence in fiscal affairs; Renzong once asked Yang Shiqi about him.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「資性強毅，人不能幹以私。

translations.literal: He replied: "Zi's nature is forceful and resolute; no one can sway him with private interest.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Zi is forceful and resolute; no one can sway him with private interest.

sentences.zh: 然蠲租詔數下不奉行，使陛下恩澤不流者，資也。」

translations.literal: Yet when edicts repeatedly came down remitting rent he did not carry them out—it is Zi who keeps Your Majesty's gracious favor from flowing forth."
translations.idiomatic: Yet when edicts remitting rent came down again and again he did not enforce them—it is Zi who keeps your grace from reaching the people."

sentences.zh: 震嘗三奉命省親，兩值關中饑，令所司出粟振之，還始以聞。

translations.literal: Zhen on three occasions received orders to visit his parents; twice he encountered famine in Guanzhong and ordered the local offices to release grain for relief, reporting only after his return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was three times ordered home to visit his parents; twice he encountered famine in Guanzhong, ordered local offices to release grain for relief, and reported only after returning.

sentences.zh: 然無學術，為禮官，不知大體。

translations.literal: Yet he had no learning; as a ritual official he did not grasp the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was unlearned; as a ritual official he lacked a sense of the larger pattern.

sentences.zh: 成祖崩，遺詔二十七日釋缞服。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor died, his testamentary edict ordered the shedding of mourning hemp on the twenty-seventh day.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu died, his testamentary edict ordered mourning hemp shed on the twenty-seventh day.

sentences.zh: 及期，震建議群臣皆易烏紗帽，黑角帶。

translations.literal: When the day came, Zhen proposed that all officials change to black gauze caps and black horn belts.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, Zhen proposed that all officials switch to black gauze caps and black horn belts.

sentences.zh: 近臣言：「仁孝皇后崩，既釋缞服，太宗易素冠布腰绖。」

translations.literal: A close minister said: "When the Renxiao Empress died, after shedding mourning hemp the Taizong Emperor changed to a plain cap with cloth waist sash."
translations.idiomatic: A close minister said, "When Empress Renxiao died, after shedding mourning hemp Taizu changed to a plain cap with cloth waist sash."

sentences.zh: 震勃然變色，詆其異己。

translations.literal: Zhen suddenly changed color in anger and slandered him as opposing his own view.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen flushed with anger and denounced him as dissenting.

sentences.zh: 仁宗黜震議，易素冠布腰绖。

translations.literal: The Renzong Emperor rejected Zhen's proposal and changed to a plain cap with cloth waist sash.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong rejected Zhen's proposal and adopted the plain cap with cloth waist sash.

sentences.zh: 洪熙元年，分遣群臣祀嶽鎮海瀆及先代帝王陵，震乞祀周文、武、成、康。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Hongxi reign, when officials were dispatched in groups to sacrifice at the sacred mountains, river gods, and seas, and at the tombs of former dynasties' emperors, Zhen requested to sacrifice to Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongxi year one, when officials were dispatched to sacrifice at sacred mountains, rivers, and seas and at former dynasties' imperial tombs, Zhen asked to sacrifice to Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 便道省母，私以妻喪柩與香帛同載。

translations.literal: Taking a convenient route to visit his mother, he privately loaded his wife's funeral bier together with incense and silks on the same cart.
translations.idiomatic: Taking a convenient route to visit his mother, he privately loaded his wife's coffin on the same cart as the incense and silks for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 祀太廟致齋，飲酒西番僧舍，大醉歸，一夕卒。

translations.literal: Having fasted before sacrificing at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, he drank wine at a Western Regions monks' lodge, returned greatly drunk, and died in a single night.
translations.idiomatic: After fasting for sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple he drank at a Western monks' lodge, returned drunk, and died overnight.

sentences.zh: 震為人佞諛傾險。

translations.literal: Zhen as a man was fawning, flattering, and treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen was fawning, flattering, and treacherous by nature.

sentences.zh: 永樂時，曹縣獻騶虞，榜葛剌國、麻林國進麒麟，震請賀。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign, Caoxian presented a zouyu, Banggela and Malin presented qilin, and Zhen requested congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle, Caoxian presented a zouyu, Banggela and Malin presented qilin, and Zhen asked that congratulations be offered.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「天下治安，無麒麒何害？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When the realm is at peace, what harm if there is no qilin?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When the realm is at peace, what harm if there is no qilin?"

sentences.zh: 貴州布政使蔣廷瓚言：「帝北征班師，詔至思南大巖山，有呼萬歲者三。」

translations.literal: The Provincial Administration Commissioner of Guizhou, Jiang Tingzan, said: "When the Emperor returned from his northern campaign, as the edict reached Dayan Mountain in Sinan, there were three cries of 'Long live the Emperor!'
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou Provincial Commissioner Jiang Tingzan said, "When the emperor returned from the northern campaign, as the edict reached Dayan Mountain in Sinan, 'Long live the emperor!' was heard three times."

sentences.zh: 震言：「此山川效靈。」

translations.literal: Zhen said: "This is the mountains and rivers manifesting their spiritual power."
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said, "This is the mountains and rivers manifesting their spiritual power."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「山谷之聲，空虛相應，理或有之。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Sounds in valleys and ravines, empty spaces answering one another—there may be reason in this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sounds in valleys echo in empty spaces—there may be reason in that.

sentences.zh: 震為國大臣，不能辯其非，又欲因之進媚，豈君子事君之道？」

translations.literal: Zhen is a great minister of the state; he cannot distinguish its falsity and moreover wishes to use it to advance flattery—is this the way a gentleman serves his ruler?"
translations.idiomatic: Zhen is a great minister of state; he cannot tell falsehood from truth and wishes to use it for flattery—is this how a gentleman serves his ruler?"

sentences.zh: 郎中周訥請封禪，震力贊之，帝責其謬。

translations.literal: Director Zhou Ne requested the Feng and Shan sacrifices; Zhen strongly endorsed this, and the Emperor rebuked the absurdity.
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhou Ne requested the Feng and Shan sacrifices; Zhen strongly endorsed the proposal, and the emperor rebuked the absurdity.

sentences.zh: 震雖累受面斥，然終不能改。

translations.literal: Though Zhen repeatedly received rebukes to his face, in the end he could not change.
translations.idiomatic: Though repeatedly rebuked to his face, Zhen never changed.

sentences.zh: 金水河、太液池冰，具樓閣龍鳳花卉狀。

translations.literal: The ice on the Jinshui River and Taiye Pool formed shapes of towers, pavilions, dragons, phoenixes, flowers, and plants.
translations.idiomatic: Ice on the Jinshui River and Taiye Pool formed shapes of towers, pavilions, dragons, phoenixes, flowers, and plants.

sentences.zh: 帝召群臣觀之。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned the officials to view them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned officials to view them.

sentences.zh: 震因請賀。

translations.literal: Zhen thereupon requested congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen again asked that congratulations be offered.

sentences.zh: 不許。

translations.literal: This was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 而隆平侯張信奏太和山五色雲見，侍郎胡濙圖上瑞光榔梅靈芝，震率群臣先後表賀雲。

translations.literal: Yet the Marquis of Longping, Zhang Xin, reported five-colored clouds appearing on Mount Taihe; Vice Minister Hu Ying presented a painting of auspicious light, langmei, and spirit fungus; and Zhen led the officials in successive memorials congratulating the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Marquis of Longping, Zhang Xin, reported five-colored clouds on Mount Taihe; Vice Minister Hu Ying presented a painting of auspicious light, langmei, and spirit fungus; and Zhen led officials in successive memorials congratulating the clouds.

sentences.zh: 成祖初巡北京，命定太子留守事宜。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor first toured Beijing, he ordered arrangements fixed for the heir apparent's stay behind to guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu first toured Beijing, he ordered arrangements for the heir apparent's stay behind.

sentences.zh: 震請常事聽太子處分，章奏分貯南京六科，回鑾日通奏。

translations.literal: Zhen requested that routine matters be left to the heir apparent's discretion, that memorials be stored separately in the six offices of the Nanjing censorate, and that on the day of the imperial return they be submitted together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen proposed that routine matters be left to the heir apparent, that memorials be filed separately in Nanjing's six censorate offices, and that on the emperor's return they be submitted together.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: Approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一年、十四年，震再請如前制。

translations.literal: In the eleventh and fourteenth years Zhen again requested the former system.
translations.idiomatic: In years eleven and fourteen Zhen again requested the same arrangement.

sentences.zh: 十七年，帝在北京，因事索章奏，侍臣言留南京。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Emperor was in Beijing; because of an affair he sought memorials, and attending ministers said they had been left in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen the emperor was in Beijing; needing memorials on a matter, attendants said they were in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 帝忘震前請，曰：「章奏宜達行在，豈禮部別有議耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor forgot Zhen's earlier request and said: "Memorials ought to reach the traveling palace—does the Ministry of Rites have some separate opinion?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor forgot Zhen's earlier proposal and said, "Memorials ought to reach the traveling palace—does the Ministry of Rites have some separate view?"

sentences.zh: 問震。

translations.literal: He questioned Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: He questioned Zhen.

sentences.zh: 震懼罪，曰：「無之，奏章當達行在。」

translations.literal: Zhen, fearing punishment, said: "There is no such thing; memorials ought to reach the traveling palace."
translations.idiomatic: Fearing punishment, Zhen said, "No such thing; memorials ought to reach the traveling palace."

sentences.zh: 三問，對如前。

translations.literal: Asked three times, he answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: Asked three times, he gave the same answer.

sentences.zh: 遂以擅留奏章，殺右給事中李能。

translations.literal: Thereupon, on the charge of arbitrarily retaining memorials, Right Supervising Secretary Li Neng was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Right Supervising Secretary Li Neng was then executed on the charge of arbitrarily retaining memorials.

sentences.zh: 眾知能冤，畏震莫敢言。

translations.literal: Everyone knew Neng was wronged, but fearing Zhen none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knew Neng was innocent, but fearing Zhen none dared speak.

sentences.zh: 尹昌隆之禍，由震構之。

translations.literal: The calamity of Yin Changlong was engineered by Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Changlong's downfall was engineered by Zhen.

sentences.zh: 事具《昌隆傳》。

translations.literal: The affair is fully set forth in the "Biography of Changlong."
translations.idiomatic: The affair is set forth in the biography of Yin Changlong.

sentences.zh: 夏原吉、方賓以言北征餉絀得罪，以震兼領戶、兵部事。

translations.literal: Xia Yuanji and Fang Bin were punished for speaking of shortfalls in northern campaign provisions; Zhen was made to oversee concurrently the affairs of the Ministries of Revenue and War.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Yuanji and Fang Bin were punished for speaking of shortfalls in northern campaign provisions; Zhen was put in charge concurrently of the Ministries of Revenue and War.

sentences.zh: 震亦自危。

translations.literal: Zhen also felt himself in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen also felt himself in peril.

sentences.zh: 帝令官校十人隨之，曰：「若震自盡，爾十人皆死。」

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered ten guard officers to follow him, saying: "If Zhen kills himself, all ten of you shall die."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered ten guard officers to follow him, saying, "If Zhen kills himself, all ten of you die."

sentences.zh: 震有精力，能強記，才足以濟其為人。

translations.literal: Zhen had vigorous energy and a powerful memory; his talent was sufficient to sustain his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had vigorous energy and a powerful memory; his talent matched his character.

sentences.zh: 凡奏事，他尚書皆執副本，又與左右侍郎更進叠奏。

translations.literal: Whenever reporting on affairs, other ministers all held duplicate copies and entered in turn with the left and right vice ministers to report in layers.
translations.idiomatic: When reporting affairs, other ministers held duplicate copies and entered in turn with their vice ministers to report in layers.

sentences.zh: 震既兼三部，奏牘益多，皆自占奏，侍郎不與也。

translations.literal: Zhen, having charge of three ministries, had ever more memorial documents; he reported on all of them himself, and the vice ministers did not participate.
translations.idiomatic: With three ministries under his charge, memorials multiplied; he reported on all of them himself while vice ministers stood aside.

sentences.zh: 情狀委曲，千緒萬端，背誦如流，未嘗有誤。

translations.literal: Circumstances winding and complex, with a thousand threads and ten thousand ends, he recited from memory like flowing water and never erred.
translations.idiomatic: Circumstances however complex, he recited from memory without a single error.

sentences.zh: 嘗扈北狩，帝見碑立沙磧中，率從臣讀其文。

translations.literal: Once, accompanying the northern hunt, the Emperor saw a stele standing in sandy desert and led his attendants in reading its text.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a northern hunt the emperor saw a stele standing in the desert and led his attendants in reading its inscription.

sentences.zh: 後一年，與諸文學臣語及碑，詔禮部遣官往錄之。

translations.literal: A year later, speaking with literary officials about the stele, he ordered the Ministry of Rites to send an officer to go record it.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, speaking with literary officials about the stele, he ordered the Ministry of Rites to send an officer to record it.

sentences.zh: 震言不須遣使，請筆劄帝前疏之。

translations.literal: Zhen said there was no need to send a messenger and requested brush and paper to transcribe it before the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen said no messenger was needed and asked for brush and paper to transcribe it before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝密使人拓其本校之，無一字脫誤者。

translations.literal: The Emperor secretly sent someone to make a rubbing and compare it; not a single character was missing or wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly had a rubbing made and compared; not a single character was missing or wrong.

sentences.zh: 子熊。

translations.literal: His son Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiong.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初立，震數於帝前乞官，至流涕。

translations.literal: When the Xuanzong Emperor had just taken the throne, Xiong repeatedly begged for office before the Emperor, even to the point of shedding tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong had just acceded, Xiong repeatedly begged for office before the emperor, even to tears.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，授兵科給事中。

translations.literal: The Emperor, having no alternative, appointed him Supervising Secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having no choice, appointed him supervising secretary in the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 李至剛，名鋼，以字行，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Li Zhigang, personal name Gang, known by his style name, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhigang, personal name Gang, known by his style, was from Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 洪武二十一年舉明經。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of the Hongwu reign he was recommended in the Mingjing examination.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongwu year twenty-one he passed the Mingjing examination.

sentences.zh: 選侍懿文太子，授禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Selected to attend the Yiwen Crown Prince, he was appointed Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Selected to attend Crown Prince Yiwen, he was appointed a director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 坐累謫戍邊，尋召為工部郎中，遷河南右參議。

translations.literal: Because of implicated guilt he was banished to garrison the frontier; before long he was recalled as Director in the Ministry of Works and transferred to Right Administrative Vice Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in a case, he was banished to frontier garrison duty; soon recalled as a director in the Ministry of Works, he was transferred to Right Administrative Vice Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河決汴堤，至剛議借王府積木，作筏濟之。

translations.literal: When the river broke the dike at Bian, Zhigang proposed borrowing stored timber from princely mansions to make rafts to ferry people across.
translations.idiomatic: When the river broke the Bian dike, Zhigang proposed borrowing stored timber from princely mansions to build rafts for rescue.

sentences.zh: 建文中，調湖廣左參議，坐事系獄。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he was transferred to Left Administrative Vice Commissioner of Huguang and was imprisoned because of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen he was transferred to Left Administrative Vice Commissioner of Huguang and imprisoned for an offense.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，左右稱其才，遂以為右通政。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor took the throne, those around him praised his talent, and he was accordingly made Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu acceded, those around him praised his talent, and he was made Right Vice Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 與修《太祖實錄》，朝夕在上左右，稱說洪武中事，甚見親信。

translations.literal: Participating in compiling the Veritable Records of the Taizu Emperor, morning and evening he was at the Emperor's side, recounting affairs of the Hongwu reign, and was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Helping compile the Veritable Records of the Taizu Emperor, he was at the emperor's side day and night recounting Hongwu-era affairs and won great trust.

sentences.zh: 尋進禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 永樂二年冊立皇太子，至剛兼左春坊大學士，直東宮講筵，與解縉後先進講。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Yongle reign, when the crown prince was installed, Zhigang was made concurrently Grand Academician of the Left Spring Office and lectured directly at the Eastern Palace lecture hall, entering to lecture before and after Xie Jin.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongle year two, when the crown prince was installed, Zhigang was made concurrently Grand Academician of the Left Spring Office and lectured at the heir apparent's hall, taking turns with Xie Jin.

sentences.zh: 已，復坐事下獄，久之得釋，降禮部郎中。

translations.literal: Later, again because of an offense he was sent down to prison; after a long time he was released and demoted to Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was later imprisoned again for an offense, released after a long interval, and demoted to director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 恨解縉，中傷之。

translations.literal: He bore hatred toward Xie Jin and slandered him.
translations.idiomatic: He resented Xie Jin and worked to slander him.

sentences.zh: 縉下獄，詞連至剛，亦坐系十余年。

translations.literal: When Jin was sent to prison, his testimony implicated Zhigang, who was also imprisoned for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin was imprisoned, his testimony implicated Zhigang, who was also held for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，得釋，復以為左通政。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor took the throne, he was released and again made Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong acceded he was released and restored as Left Vice Commissioner of Transmission.

sentences.zh: 給事中梁盛等劾至剛輩十余人，當大行晏駕，不宿公署，飲酒食肉，恬無戚容。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Liang Sheng and others impeached Zhigang and more than ten of his kind: when the late emperor was passing away, they did not lodge in the public offices, but drank wine and ate meat with untroubled faces showing no grief.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liang Sheng and others impeached Zhigang and more than ten colleagues: when the late emperor lay dying they did not stay in the public offices but drank and ate meat with untroubled faces.

sentences.zh: 帝念至剛先朝舊人，出為興化知府，時年已七十。

translations.literal: The Emperor, mindful that Zhigang was an old man of the former reign, sent him out as prefect of Xinghua; he was then already seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Mindful that Zhigang was a holdover from the previous reign, the emperor posted him as prefect of Xinghua at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 再歲，歿於官。

translations.literal: Two years later he died while holding office.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he died in office.

sentences.zh: 至剛為人敏給，能治繁劇，善傅會。

translations.literal: Zhigang as a man was quick and resourceful, able to handle complex and urgent affairs, and skilled at adapting to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigang was quick and resourceful, able to handle complex affairs, and skilled at adapting to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 首發建都北平議，請禁言事者挾私，成祖從之。

translations.literal: He was the first to raise the proposal to make the capital at Beiping and requested that those who spoke on affairs be forbidden to harbor private motives; the Chengzu Emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: He was the first to propose making Beiping the capital and asked that memorialists be forbidden to advance private motives; Chengzu agreed.

sentences.zh: 既得上心，務為佞諛。

translations.literal: Having won the Emperor's heart, he strove to be fawning and flattering.
translations.idiomatic: Having won the emperor's favor, he strove to flatter.

sentences.zh: 嘗言太祖忌辰，宜效宋制，令僧道誦經。

translations.literal: He once said that on the anniversary of the Taizu Emperor's death one ought to follow the Song system and order monks and Daoists to chant sutras.
translations.idiomatic: He once proposed that on Taizu's death anniversary the Song practice be followed and monks and Daoists ordered to chant sutras.

sentences.zh: 山東野蠶成繭，至剛請賀。

translations.literal: When wild silkworms in Shandong formed cocoons, Zhigang requested congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When wild silkworms in Shandong formed cocoons, Zhigang asked that congratulations be offered.

sentences.zh: 陜西進瑞麥，至剛率百官賀。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi presented auspicious wheat, Zhigang led the hundred officials in congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi presented auspicious wheat, Zhigang led the officials in congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝皆不聽。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not heed any of these.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused every proposal.

sentences.zh: 中官使真臘，從者逃三人，國王以國中三人補之。

translations.literal: A palace eunuch was sent to Zhenla; three of his attendants fled, and the king of the country replaced them with three men from within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch was sent to Zhenla; three attendants fled, and the king replaced them with three subjects of his own.

sentences.zh: 帝令遣還，至剛言：「中國三人，安知非彼私匿？」

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered them sent back; Zhigang said: "These three men from China—how do we know they are not persons he secretly concealed?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered them sent back; Zhigang said, "These three Chinese men—how do we know they are not persons he secretly concealed?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕以至誠待內外，何用逆詐。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I treat inner and outer with utmost sincerity—what need is there for contrary suspicion?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I treat all with utmost sincerity—what need for contrary suspicion?"

sentences.zh: 所建白多不用。

translations.literal: Most of what he proposed was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his proposals went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 妻父麗重法，至剛為乞免。

translations.literal: His wife's father, Li, was sentenced to heavy punishment; Zhigang begged exemption for him.
translations.idiomatic: His father-in-law Li was sentenced to heavy punishment; Zhigang begged exemption.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「獄輕重，外人何以知之？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Whether a case is light or heavy—how can outsiders know?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Whether a case is light or heavy—how can outsiders know?"

sentences.zh: 至剛曰：「都御史黃信為臣言。」

translations.literal: Zhigang said: "Censor-in-Chief Huang Xin told me on my behalf."
translations.idiomatic: Zhigang said, "Censor-in-Chief Huang Xin told me."

sentences.zh: 帝怒，誅信。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and executed Xin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and executed Xin.

sentences.zh: 初，至剛與解縉交甚厚。

translations.literal: At first Zhigang and Xie Jin were on very close terms.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhigang and Xie Jin were close friends.

sentences.zh: 帝書大臣姓名十人，命縉疏其人品，言至剛不端。

translations.literal: The Emperor wrote the names of ten great ministers and ordered Jin to set forth their characters, saying Zhigang was not upright.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote ten ministers' names and ordered Jin to assess their characters, calling Zhigang not upright.

sentences.zh: 縉謫廣西，至剛遂奏其怨望，改謫交阯。

translations.literal: Jin was banished to Guangxi; Zhigang thereupon memorialized that he harbored resentment, and the banishment was changed to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was banished to Guangxi; Zhigang then memorialized that he harbored resentment, and the banishment was changed to Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 方賓，錢塘人。

translations.literal: Fang Bin was a native of Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Bin was from Qiantang.

sentences.zh: 洪武時由太學生試兵部郎中。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign, through the status of a student of the Imperial Academy he was tried out as Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongwu he entered service as an Imperial Academy student and was given a probationary appointment as director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 建文中，署應天府事。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign he acted in the affairs of Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jianwen he acted in the affairs of Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 坐罪戍廣東。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was banished to garrison Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Convicted of an offense, he was banished to garrison duty in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 以茹常薦，召復官。

translations.literal: On Ru Chang's recommendation he was summoned and restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: On Ru Chang's recommendation he was recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 成祖入京師，賓與侍郎劉俊等迎附，特見委用，進兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Chengzu Emperor entered the capital, Bin together with Vice Minister Liu Jun and others went out to welcome and attach themselves; he was specially entrusted and employed, and was advanced to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzu entered the capital, Bin with Vice Minister Liu Jun and others went out to welcome him and was specially entrusted, rising to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四年，俊以尚書出征黎利，賓理部事，有幹才，應務不滯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Jun went out as Minister on campaign against Li Li; Bin managed the ministry's affairs, had administrative talent, and handled business without delay.
translations.idiomatic: In year four Jun marched against Li Li as minister; Bin managed the ministry with administrative talent and handled affairs without delay.

sentences.zh: 性警敏，能揣上意，見知於帝，頗恃寵貪恣。

translations.literal: His nature was alert and keen; he could gauge the ruler's intent, was recognized by the Emperor, and rather relied on favor to be greedy and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Alert and keen, he could gauge the emperor's intent, won favor, and rather relied on it to be greedy and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 七年進尚書，扈從北京，兼掌行在吏部事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to Minister, accompanied the court to Beijing, and concurrently managed the affairs of the traveling palace Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven he was promoted to minister, accompanied the court to Beijing, and concurrently managed the traveling palace Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 明年從北征，與學士胡廣、金幼孜、楊榮，侍郎金純並與機密。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the northern campaign and together with Academicians Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, and Yang Rong, and Vice Minister Jin Chun, shared in confidential matters.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he joined the northern campaign and with Academicians Hu Guang, Jin Youzi, and Yang Rong and Vice Minister Jin Chun shared confidential counsel.

sentences.zh: 自後帝北巡，賓輒扈從。

translations.literal: From then on whenever the Emperor toured the north, Bin always accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, whenever the emperor toured the north, Bin always accompanied him.

sentences.zh: 十九年，議親征。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year a personal campaign was discussed.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen a personal campaign was discussed.

sentences.zh: 尚書夏原吉、吳中、呂震與賓共議，宜且休兵養民。

translations.literal: Ministers Xia Yuanji, Wu Zhong, Lu Zhen, and Bin together discussed that it would be better for the time being to rest the army and nourish the people.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Xia Yuanji, Wu Zhong, Lu Zhen, and Bin agreed it would be better to rest the army and nourish the people for the time being.

sentences.zh: 未奏，會帝召賓，賓言糧餉不足，召原吉，亦以不給對。

translations.literal: Before they could memorialize, it happened that the Emperor summoned Bin; Bin said provisions were insufficient, and when Yuanji was summoned he too answered that supplies would not suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could memorialize, the emperor summoned Bin, who said provisions were insufficient; Yuanji was summoned and gave the same answer.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遣原吉視糧開平，旋召還下獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, sent Yuanji to inspect grain at Kaiping, then soon recalled him and sent him down to prison.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, sent Yuanji to inspect grain at Kaiping, then recalled him and imprisoned him.

sentences.zh: 賓方提調靈濟宮。

translations.literal: Bin was then supervising arrangements at the Lingji Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bin was then supervising arrangements at the Lingji Palace.

sentences.zh: 中使進香至，語賓以帝怒。

translations.literal: When a palace messenger arrived to offer incense, he told Bin of the Emperor's anger.
translations.idiomatic: When a palace messenger arrived to offer incense, he told Bin of the emperor's anger.

sentences.zh: 賓懼，自縊死。

translations.literal: Bin, in fear, hanged himself and died.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Bin hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 帝實無意殺賓，聞賓死，乃益怒，戮其屍。

translations.literal: The Emperor in fact had no intention of killing Bin; hearing Bin had died, he grew only angrier and desecrated his corpse.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had not intended to kill Bin; hearing of his death he grew only angrier and desecrated the corpse.

sentences.zh: 中勤敏多計算。

translations.literal: Zhong was diligent, keen, and skilled in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Zhong was diligent, keen, and skilled in calculation.

sentences.zh: 先後在工部二十余年，北京宮殿，長、獻、景三陵，皆中所營造。

translations.literal: He was in the Ministry of Works for more than twenty years altogether; the palaces of Beijing and the three mausoleums of Chang, Xian, and Jing were all constructed under his direction.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than twenty years in the Ministry of Works; the Beijing palaces and the Chang, Xian, and Jing mausoleums were all built under his direction.

sentences.zh: 職務填委，規畫井然。

translations.literal: His duties were piled high, yet his planning was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Though his duties were piled high, his planning was orderly.

sentences.zh: 然不恤工匠，又湛於聲色，時論鄙之。

translations.literal: Yet he did not show compassion for artisans, and moreover was steeped in music and women; contemporary opinion despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he showed no compassion for artisans and was steeped in music and women; contemporary opinion despised him.

sentences.zh: 劉觀，雄縣人。

translations.literal: Liu Guan was a native of Xiong County.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guan was from Xiong County.

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of the Hongwu reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Hongwu year eighteen.

sentences.zh: 授太谷縣丞，以薦擢監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Taigu County and, on recommendation, was promoted to Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed assistant magistrate of Taigu County and, on recommendation, promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 三十年遷署左僉都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to act as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty he was made acting Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 坐事下獄，尋釋。

translations.literal: Because of an offense he was sent down to prison and before long released.
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned for an offense, he was soon released.

sentences.zh: 出為嘉興知府，丁父憂去。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Jiaxing and left on mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as prefect of Jiaxing and left on mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 仁宗嗣位，兼太子賓客，旋加太子少保，給二俸。

translations.literal: When the Renzong Emperor succeeded to the throne, he was made concurrently Guest of the Heir Apparent, and soon after added as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with two salaries granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Renzong succeeded to the throne, he was made concurrently Guest of the Heir Apparent and soon added as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent with two salaries.

sentences.zh: 時大理少卿弋謙數言事，帝厭其繁瑣。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Minister of Justice Yi Qian repeatedly spoke on affairs, and the Emperor was weary of his tediousness.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Justice Yi Qian then spoke repeatedly on affairs, and the emperor grew weary of his tediousness.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂震、大理卿虞謙希旨劾奏，觀復令十四道御史論其誣妄，以是為輿論所鄙。

translations.literal: Minister Lu Zhen and Minister of Justice Yu Qian, seeking to please the Emperor's intent, impeached and memorialized; Guan further ordered the censors of the fourteen circuits to discuss his falsehood and presumption, and for this was despised in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lu Zhen and Minister of Justice Yu Qian, seeking to please the emperor, impeached him; Guan further ordered censors of the fourteen circuits to denounce his falsehood, and for this was despised in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 時未有官妓之禁。

translations.literal: At that time there was not yet a prohibition on official courtesans.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was not yet a prohibition on official courtesans.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，臣僚宴樂，以奢相尚，歌妓滿前。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xuande reign, when officials feasted and made music, they vied in luxury, with singing girls filling the space before them.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xuande, when officials feasted they vied in luxury, with singing girls before them.

sentences.zh: 觀私納賄賂，而諸御史亦貪縱無忌。

translations.literal: Guan privately accepted bribes, and the various censors also were greedy and unrestrained without fear.
translations.idiomatic: Guan privately accepted bribes, and the censors too were greedy and unrestrained.

sentences.zh: 三年六月朝罷，帝召大學士楊士奇、楊榮至文華門，諭曰：「祖宗時，朝臣謹飭。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, when court was dismissed, the Emperor summoned Grand Academicians Yang Shiqi and Yang Rong to the Wenhua Gate and instructed them: "In the time of the ancestors, court ministers were careful and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year three, after court was dismissed, the emperor summoned Grand Academicians Yang Shiqi and Yang Rong to the Wenhua Gate and said, "Under the founding emperors, court ministers were careful and restrained.

sentences.zh: 年來貪濁成風，何也？」

translations.literal: In recent years greed and corruption have become the fashion—why is this?"
translations.idiomatic: In recent years greed and corruption have become the fashion—why is this?"

sentences.zh: 士奇對曰：「永樂末已有之，今為甚耳。」

translations.literal: Shiqi replied: "At the end of the Yongle reign it already existed; now it is only more severe."
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi replied, "It already existed at the end of Yongle; now it is only worse."

sentences.zh: 榮曰：「永樂時，無逾方賓。」

translations.literal: Rong said: "During the Yongle reign, none exceeded Fang Bin."
translations.idiomatic: Rong said, "Under Yongle, none exceeded Fang Bin."

sentences.zh: 帝問：「今日誰最甚者？」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked: "Today who is the most severe?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Who is worst today?"

sentences.zh: 榮對曰：「劉觀。」

translations.literal: Rong replied: "Liu Guan."
translations.idiomatic: Rong replied, "Liu Guan."

sentences.zh: 又問：「誰可代者？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "Who can replace him?"
translations.idiomatic: He asked again, "Who can replace him?"

sentences.zh: 士奇、榮薦通政使顧佐。

translations.literal: Shiqi and Rong recommended Commissioner of Transmission Gu Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi and Rong recommended Commissioner of Transmission Gu Zuo.

sentences.zh: 帝乃出觀視河道，以佐為右都御史。

translations.literal: The Emperor then sent Guan out to inspect the river works and made Zuo Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent Guan out to inspect the river works and made Zuo Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 於是御史張循理等交章劾觀，並其子輻諸贓汙不法事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Censor Zhang Xunli and others submitted successive memorials impeaching Guan, together with his son Fu on various matters of corruption and unlawful conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zhang Xunli and others then submitted successive memorials impeaching Guan and his son Fu for corruption and unlawful conduct.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，逮觀父子，以彈章示之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry, arrested Guan father and son, and showed them the impeachment documents.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious, arrested father and son, and showed them the impeachment documents.

sentences.zh: 觀疏辯。

translations.literal: Guan memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Guan memorialized in defense.

sentences.zh: 帝益怒，出廷臣先後密奏，中有枉法受賕至千金者。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew angrier still and produced the court ministers' successive secret memorials, among which were cases of perverting the law and accepting bribes up to a thousand taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angrier still and produced ministers' secret memorials citing perversion of law and bribes up to a thousand taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 觀引伏，遂下錦衣衛獄。

translations.literal: Guan confessed, and was thereupon sent down to the Brocade Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Guan confessed and was sent to the Brocade Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 明年將置重典。

translations.literal: The next year he was to be subjected to heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The next year heavy punishment was planned.

sentences.zh: 士奇、榮乞貸其死。

translations.literal: Shiqi and Rong begged that his life be spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi and Rong begged that his life be spared.

sentences.zh: 乃謫輻戍遼東，而命觀隨往，觀竟客死。

translations.literal: Fu was then banished to garrison Liaodong, and Guan was ordered to go with him; Guan in the end died as a guest in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was banished to garrison Liaodong and Guan ordered to accompany him; Guan died in exile.

sentences.zh: 七年，士奇請命風憲官考察奏罷有司之貪汙者，帝曰：「然。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Shiqi requested that surveillance officials be ordered to investigate and memorialize for dismissal those local officials who were corrupt; the Emperor said: "So be it.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven Shiqi asked that surveillance officials investigate and memorialize for dismissal corrupt local officials; the emperor said, "So be it.

sentences.zh: 向使不罷劉觀，風憲安得肅。」

translations.literal: Had Liu Guan not been removed, how could surveillance discipline have been restored?"
translations.idiomatic: Had Liu Guan not been removed, how could surveillance discipline have been restored?"

sentences.zh: 贊曰：成祖封茹常，以事太祖有功。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Chengzu Emperor enfeoffed Ru Chang because in serving the Taizu Emperor he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Chengzu enfeoffed Ru Chang for merit in serving Taizu.

sentences.zh: 然考之，未有所表見，意史軼之歟？

translations.literal: Yet on examination, nothing is manifested—might the history have lost it?
translations.idiomatic: Yet on examination nothing is recorded—has the history lost it?

sentences.zh: 嚴震直之於廣西，張紞之於雲南，治效卓然。

translations.literal: Yan Zhenzhi in Guangxi and Zhang Dan in Yunnan had governing achievements that stood out.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenzhi in Guangxi and Zhang Dan in Yunnan achieved outstanding governance.

sentences.zh: 王鈍、鄭賜為方伯、監司，聲績頗著。

translations.literal: Wang Dun and Zheng Ci as provincial governors and surveillance commissioners had reputations and records that were quite notable.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun and Zheng Ci as provincial governors and surveillance commissioners won notable reputations.

sentences.zh: 至其晚節，皆不克自振，惜夫。

translations.literal: Yet in their later years none could rouse themselves—it is regrettable.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in their later years none could rouse themselves—a pity.

sentences.zh: 郭資、呂震之徒，有幹濟才，而操行無取。

translations.literal: Men such as Guo Zi and Lu Zhen had talent for practical achievement, yet their conduct was not admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Guo Zi and Lu Zhen had talent for practical achievement, yet their conduct was not admirable.

sentences.zh: 李至剛之險，吳中、劉觀之墨，又不足道矣。

translations.literal: Li Zhigang's treachery, Wu Zhong's and Liu Guan's corruption—these are not even worth mentioning.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhigang's treachery and the corruption of Wu Zhong and Liu Guan are not even worth mentioning.
